fr.elements: Main Building; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Internal Drive Aisle; Internal Drive Aisle; Access Road; Landscaped Area; Landscaped Area; Walkway; Open Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access point with clearly visible address signage readable from the approaching road in both directions.

• Post a site map near the access point showing building location, drive aisle routes, and any dead-end areas to orient arriving responders.

• Keep both internal drive aisles clear of parked vehicles and equipment to allow emergency vehicles to reach the building and reposition if needed.

• Trim dense vegetation along drive aisles to maintain clear sightlines for emergency vehicles approaching the building.

• Mark the farthest point of each drive aisle clearly so responders know where vehicle access ends and foot travel begins.

• Identify and mark any secondary foot approach to the rear of the building so responders are aware of available routes when vehicle access to the rear is not possible.

wildfire.conditions: Large Paved Area; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Scattered Trees; Brush Area; Vegetation Near Building; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Multiple Access Routes; Scattered Shrubs; Ground Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin the brush area to reduce the concentration of vegetation closest to any buildings or structures.
• Trim lower branches on tree clusters and scattered trees that are growing near structures or overhanging rooflines.
• Clear ground vegetation and scattered shrubs that are growing directly against building walls or foundations.
• Keep the large paved area clear of dead leaves, debris, and any vegetation growing through surface cracks or along edges near buildings.
• Maintain the multiple access routes free of vegetation encroachment along travel lanes and shoulders.
• Preserve the existing open separation between landscaped vegetation and buildings — do not allow new plantings to close that gap.
